title: HE LOOKED AGAIN.
paragraphs: HE LOOKED AGAIN.

Just a glance.
Just a rooftop.
Just a quiet night in Jerusalem.
But history changed in that second look.
The Bible tells it with chilling simplicity in Book of 2 Samuel 11.
King David should have been at war with his men.
Instead…
He stayed home.

One evening he walked on the palace roof.
The breeze moved across the city.
Torches flickered below.
Then he saw her.
Bathsheba.
Bathing.
Scripture says she was very beautiful.
And David looked.
Then—
He looked again.
That second look was the doorway.
Sin rarely begins with a roar.

It begins with a pause.
A curiosity.
A lingering glance.
David didn’t fall in a battlefield.
He fell in a moment of unchecked desire.

He sent messengers.
He took her.
She conceived.
And to cover the scandal…
An innocent man died.
Uriah the Hittite was sent to the front lines to be killed.

A king.
A hero.
A man after God’s own heart.
Collapsed under the weight of one unchecked moment.
But the story does not end in darkness.
Because God sent a prophet.
Nathan the Prophet walked into the palace and spoke truth that cut like a blade.
David broke.

Not defensiveness.
Not excuses.
Repentance.

Out of that broken moment came one of the most raw prayers ever written in Scripture—
Psalm 51.
“Create in me a clean heart, O God.”
Here is the Gospel tension:

David’s sin was real.
People were hurt.
Consequences remained.
But God’s mercy was greater.
Generations later, from David’s broken lineage, a Savior would come—
Jesus Christ.
The King who never took a second look at sin.
The King who died to cleanse ours.
Maybe your fall didn’t begin with a shout either.

Maybe it began with a glance.
A message.
A curiosity you didn’t shut down.
Listen carefully.
Grace still speaks.
The same God who restored David still restores sinners who repent and run to Christ.
Not perfection.
Repentance.
That is the doorway back.
Today, guard the second look.
Because the enemy wins there.
But so can holiness.
Turn your eyes to Jesus.
And let grace rewrite the story.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
